## In-Class Agenda

- Trusting others to do the math and large scale data cleaning
- Using data found on the web
- Debate: How does our focus or question shape the data we create? How can we make these assumptions visible?

## Assigned Materials

- Lincoln, Matthew D. “Confabulation in the Humanities.” *Matthew Lincoln, PhD* (blog), March 21, 2015. [https://matthewlincoln.net/2015/03/21/confabulation-in-the-humanities.html](https://matthewlincoln.net/2015/03/21/confabulation-in-the-humanities.html).
- Mullen, Lincoln. “Isn’t It Obvious?” *Lincolnmullen.Com* (blog), January 10, 2018. [https://lincolnmullen.com/blog/isnt-it-obvious/](https://lincolnmullen.com/blog/isnt-it-obvious/).
- D’Ignazio, Catherine, and Lauren F. Klein. “On Rational, Scientific, Objective Viewpoints from Mythical, Imaginary, Impossible Standpoints.” In *Data Feminism*, 73–96. The MIT Press, 2020. [https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/11805.003.0005](https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/11805.003.0005).
